title: JANUS Engine R0M3 — motor/regenerator crossover and back-EMF map
purpose: Prove when the Axle magnetic machine is consuming battery energy, merely reducing motor demand through hydraulic assistance, or actually regenerating independently sourced mechanical energy into the battery.
pass_rules: Back EMF increases repeatably with RPM for frozen field geometry.
Applying an electrical generator load produces measurable opposing shaft torque consistent with energy conservation.
A regenerative claim requires independently measured external shaft/hydraulic work or a measured decrease in rotor kinetic energy.
Battery-motor-only operation must never credit same-shaft regeneration as new generated energy.
The zero-current crossover must be identified experimentally: hydraulic/external torque carries the rotating load with AFPM electrical torque approximately zero.
Above crossover, positive battery charging is credited only after inverter, bearing, eddy-current and hydraulic accounting closes.
design_target: One coreless/slotless AFPM unit should start the Axle, control RPM, recover braking energy and automatically regenerate whenever genuine external mechanical torque exceeds process drag.
next_after_pass: Feed measured motor/generator efficiency and crossover maps into startup-battery sizing and full JANUS net-energy simulation.
